name: Medpill

lead: Medpill is a term from looksmaxxing forums, formed on the model of blackpill and redpill. In the threads where it appears it refers to the claim that Mediterranean or dark-featured men, with darker hair, eyes and skin tones, are attractive to women and outperform fairer Nordic-type features.

Members use it to point to anecdotes, such as a woman praising a tanned, dark-haired partner, and to argue that colouring matters in how people are perceived. It is a community claim rather than a researched concept.

paras: In practice it appears as forum threads sharing anecdotes and photographs. Members who accept the idea may talk about tanning, hair colour and darker-toned styling, though the term mostly functions as a discussion label.

The label is discussed in threads that mix appearance talk with ethnic generalisations, and attractiveness research reports that preferences vary by person and culture. It carries no direct physical risks; tanning has well-documented skin-cancer risk.

lead: Medpill is slang used on looksmax.org and related forums. In the threads where it is used, it denotes the belief that Mediterranean and dark-featured men are preferred by women over fairer, Nordic-type men [1].

The format follows other pill terms: a thread presents a story or anecdote, such as a woman describing her partner's tanned skin, green eyes and dark hair, as the revelation, and members discuss whether colouring helps attractiveness [1]. Participants usually treat it as part of broader debate on how ethnicity and colouring affect perception.
infobox: Looksmaxxing forums, modelled on redpill and blackpill

paras: The term appears in forum thread titles that frame a story as a revelation, with members adding their own anecdotes and photos in replies [1].

Proponents say anecdotes, such as a woman bragging about a tanned, dark-haired partner, show that fair colouring is not the only preferred look [1]. Critics within the forums and outside them point out that such cases are individual and that preferences vary.

lore.intro: On looksmax.org the term appears in thread titles presenting anecdotes about colouring and attraction [1].
